preconditions.description: The size of the set S, m, is between 1 and 1000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(s) == m and all(1 <= x <= 10**6 for x in s)
preconditions.description: The input list s contains exactly m integers, each between 1 and 10^6 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(s[i] < s[i+1] for i in range(len(s)-1))
preconditions.description: The elements of the set S are given in strictly increasing order.

postconditions.expression: output_lines[0] == '-1' or (len(output_lines) == 2 and output_lines[0].isdigit() and int(output_lines[0]) <= 4000)
postconditions.description: The output is either a single line containing -1, or two lines where the first line is an integer n not exceeding 4000.

postconditions.expression: output_lines[0] == '-1' or (all(1 <= int(x) <= 10**6 for x in output_lines[1].split()) and len(output_lines[1].split()) == int(output_lines[0]))
postconditions.description: If a solution is provided, the second line contains exactly n integers, each between 1 and 10^6 inclusive.

postconditions.expression: output_lines[0] == '-1' or (set(gcd_range(a, i, j) for i in range(len(a)) for j in range(i, len(a))) == set(s))
postconditions.description: If a solution is provided, the set of all GCDs of contiguous subarrays of the output sequence a is exactly equal to the input set S.

postconditions.expression: output_lines[0] != '-1' or (set(gcd_range(a, i, j) for i in range(len(a)) for j in range(i, len(a))) != set(s) for a in [list(map(int, output_lines[1].split())) if len(output_lines) > 1 else []])
postconditions.description: If the output is -1, it implies that no sequence exists that produces the set S (though the code must ensure this is true, the postcondition here validates the negative case logic).
